title: 50,000 Vanars, 3,500 Extras, and the Man Who Made Baahubali Look Small: Inside Rajamouli's Varanasi
excerpt: SS Rajamouli just showed the first footage of his mythological epic at a Paris cinematheque — and now he's building the biggest battle sequence in Indian cinema history, with Mahesh Babu at the centre of it.
body:
Here is what we know: on June 27, at La Cinémathèque Française in Paris, **SS Rajamouli** stood before a European audience and showed them the very first footage from **Varanasi**, the mythological action epic that has been in production for the better part of two years. The room applauded. The footage has not leaked. And the man who built Baahubali's waterfall and RRR's bridge is now preparing to shoot a battle scene that makes both of those look like warm-ups.

According to a report by Mid-Day, Rajamouli will resume shooting in Hyderabad starting July 7 — and the sequence he's filming is unlike anything attempted in Indian cinema. The set will feature **3,500 junior artists** performing live on location. That number alone would make it one of the largest crowd sequences ever filmed in India. But here's where it gets insane: in post-production, those 3,500 performers will be digitally multiplied using advanced VFX to create an army of **50,000 vanars on screen simultaneously**.

Fifty. Thousand.

## The Scale Only Rajamouli Would Attempt

To put that number in context: the climactic battle in *Baahubali: The Conclusion* featured roughly 5,000 VFX soldiers. The Naatu Naatu sequence in *RRR* that won the Oscar was famously shot with 500 dancers. Rajamouli has always been a filmmaker who thinks in multiples of ten — but a 50,000-strong Vanar army represents a leap that even by his standards feels almost reckless in its ambition.

The preparation has been meticulous. The crew has reportedly been working for weeks to coordinate the logistics of the shoot — choreographing the movements of thousands of performers, designing the motion-capture and plate photography that will serve as the foundation for the VFX expansion, and building sets that can accommodate the sheer physical scale of the sequence.



> **"**Prithviraj Sukumaran** rounds out the lead cast, adding his considerable dramatic weight to what is shaping up to be one of the most stacked ensembles in Indian cinema history."**


**Mahesh Babu**, in his most physically demanding role to date, will be at the centre of this battle. The Telugu superstar — making what is effectively his pan-India debut under Rajamouli's direction — has been training for the role for over a year, and early whispers from the set suggest he has transformed himself in a way audiences have never seen.

## Priyanka Chopra and a Mythological Universe

**Priyanka Chopra Jonas** stars alongside Mahesh Babu in what is her most significant Indian film role in nearly a decade. After building one of the most valuable celebrity brands on the planet — Forbes India recently valued her empire at over ₹2,500 crore — her return to Indian cinema in a Rajamouli film feels like a statement: this is the project worthy of bringing her back.

**Prithviraj Sukumaran** rounds out the lead cast, adding his considerable dramatic weight to what is shaping up to be one of the most stacked ensembles in Indian cinema history.

The film's narrative is described as a grand mythological action epic that explores the adventures of its protagonist across different timelines. Details remain closely guarded — Rajamouli is famously secretive about his scripts — but the Vanar army battle, the mythological framework, and the time-travel elements suggest something far more ambitious than a straightforward period film.

## Paris Was Just the Beginning

The La Cinémathèque Française screening on June 27 was Rajamouli's way of introducing Varanasi to the global film community on his own terms. No leaked teaser, no social media rollout — just the director, the footage, and one of the world's most respected film institutions. The reception was reportedly rapturous, and it has set off a wave of anticipation among international film circles that mirrors what happened when early footage from *Baahubali* began circulating in 2014.

For the Indian diaspora, the stakes are personal. Rajamouli's films don't just perform at the box office abroad — they become events. *RRR* screenings in American multiplexes turned into spontaneous dance parties. *Baahubali 2* grossed over ₹500 crore overseas. Varanasi, with its mythological canvas and global-scale VFX ambitions, is being positioned as the film that could take Indian cinema's international footprint to its next frontier.

## The Road to April 2027

Varanasi is currently slated for a theatrical release in **April 2027**. The July shoot in Hyderabad will focus on the Vanar army battle — the film's most complex and technically demanding sequence — and post-production is expected to stretch deep into next year as the VFX team works to bring those 50,000 digital warriors to life.

If the history of Rajamouli's career is any guide, they'll get it done. The man who was told a waterfall fortress was impossible, who was told a dance number couldn't win an Oscar, who was told Indian cinema couldn't compete at the global scale, has spent two decades proving that the only limit is the size of the vision.

Fifty thousand vanars. One filmmaker. The biggest canvas Indian cinema has ever attempted.

And he's just getting started.
